item.title: Anomalies for compact simple Lie groups via $G$-kernels for loop group nets
item.description: arXiv:2610.23321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a compact simply connected simple Lie group and $k \geq 1$. Jump loops give an outer homomorphism $\theta_k$ from $G$ to the outer automorphisms of the local factor of the level-$k$ loop group net, which is the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. We show that its Sutherland obstruction is $k$ times the positive basic class in $H^3_{\mathrm{Borel}}(G, \mathbb{T}) \cong H^{4}(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ and that $\theta_k$ is faithful, so it is a $G$-kernel. Central elements act by the outer automorphisms of the simple currents. In types A, D, E the level-one class is computed by comparing maximal-torus jump loops with the lattice $\alpha$-induction construction of the companion paper on both current and charged generators, followed by integral degree-four Cartan restriction. Higher levels follow by tensor additivity, and the remaining types by restriction along index-one embeddings into simply laced groups. As a consequence, for every compact simply connected semisimple $G$, every class in $H^4(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ is the obstruction of a $G$-kernel on the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Bischoff, Pradyut Karmakar

item.title: On Mbekhta's conjecture and pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.23229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give negative answers to Mbekhta's conjecture \cite[p.~261]{Mbekhta} and to a related conjecture on pseudo-B-Fredholm operators \cite[p.~202]{AZO}. A sufficient condition for pseudo-Fredholmness on Banach spaces is established. It yields a characterization on Hilbert spaces in terms of the closedness of $\cc(T)$, $\cc(T)+\qn(T)$ and $\Ran(T)+\qn(T)$, as well as characterizations of pseudo-B-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Weyl operators on Banach spaces. A counterexample on a separable Banach space shows that the three closedness conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness in general. We also construct two operators having the same analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and kernels and ranges of all powers, although only one is pseudo-Fredholm. Moreover, a semi-B-Fredholm operator on a Banach space need not be a direct sum of a semi-Fredholm operator and a nilpotent operator, answering the question raised in \cite[p.~113]{AznayKato2023}. Finally, the three closedness conditions in the Hilbert-space characterization are shown to be independent.
item.dc:creator: Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi

item.title: On the complexification of $ q $-deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the quantised algebra of functions on a simply connected compact semisimple Lie group, we study the relationship between the primitive spectrum, topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on Hilbert spaces, and quantum holomorphic evaluations induced via the Drinfeld double. In terms of the Joseph stratification of the primitive spectrum, we prove a sharp dichotomy: primitive ideals in homogeneous strata always arise as kernels of topologically irreducible representations by bounded operators on a Hilbert space, whereas those in inhomogeneous strata do not admit any such realisations. We further show that, unlike in the classical situation, quantum holomorphic evaluations typically fail to be topologically irreducible, and that their kernels do not determine the primitive spectrum. Finally, we describe the Iwasawa decomposition of the Drinfeld double in terms of polynomial functions, extending work by Podle\'s-Woronowicz for the quantum Lorentz group to all complex semisimple quantum groups, and clarifying the structure of quantum holomorphic evaluations.
item.dc:creator: Heon Lee, Christian Voigt

item.title: MIP*=RE
item.description: arXiv:2001.04383v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the class MIP* of languages that can be decided by a classical verifier interacting with multiple all-powerful quantum provers sharing entanglement is equal to the class RE of recursively enumerable languages. Our proof builds upon the quantum low-degree test of (Natarajan and Vidick, FOCS 2018) and the classical low-individual degree test of (Ji, et al., 2020) by integrating recent developments from (Natarajan and Wright, FOCS 2019) and combining them with the recursive compression framework of (Fitzsimons et al., STOC 2019). An immediate byproduct of our result is that there is an efficient reduction from the Halting Problem to the problem of deciding whether a two-player nonlocal game has entangled value $1$ or at most $1/2$. Using a known connection, undecidability of the entangled value implies a negative answer to Tsirelson's problem: we show, by providing an explicit example, that the closure $C_{qa}$ of the set of quantum tensor product correlations is strictly included in the set $C_{qc}$ of quantum commuting correlations. Following work of (Fritz, Rev. Math. Phys. 2012) and (Junge et al., J. Math. Phys. 2011) our results provide a refutation of Connes' embedding conjecture from the theory of von Neumann algebras.
item.dc:creator: Zhengfeng Ji, Anand Natarajan, Thomas Vidick, John Wright, Henry Yuen

item.title: On the quotient matrix and its distinct eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2604.03194v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be an $n\times n$ matrix partitioned into blocks according to a partition $P=\{C_{1},\dots,C_{\ell}\}$ of its index set, and let $Q$ be the corresponding equitable quotient. We study when $Q$ contains every distinct eigenvalue of $M$, so that the distinct spectral data of a large structured matrix can be recovered from a lower-order quotient. We first correct the distinction between a coarsest equitable partition and a minimum-order quotient that captures all distinct eigenvalues. We then establish an exact block-lifting construction with characteristic polynomial $\chi_M(x)=\chi_Q(x)\prod_i(x-\theta_i)^{|C_i|-1}$, derive multiplicity-design consequences, and give a necessary and sufficient eigenspace criterion for quotient capture. Further results quantify automatic capture through geometric multiplicity and describe exact spectral factors generated by twin cells in graph matrices. Applications to adjacency, weighted adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, distance, and distance-based Laplacian matrices are validated, including minimal one-cell refinements that recover eigenvalues hidden by collapsed twin classes.
item.dc:creator: Bilal Ahmad Rather, Jianfeng Wang, Zhaoxi Li

item.title: Maximal subgroups of topological full groups arising from factor maps and subgroupoids
item.description: arXiv:2609.33118v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct maximal subgroups of topological full groups and their commutator subgroups using factor maps and wide open subgroupoids of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit spaces, assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness. For two-to-one coverings and prime factor maps with principal target and fibers of cardinality at most two, surjectivity and injectivity of the same induced map on full-group abelianizations characterize maximality of the factor full group and factor commutator subgroup, respectively. For subgroupoids arising from prime-order cyclic actions free on the unit space, the normalizer of the smaller commutator subgroup in the ambient full group is a semidirect product, maximal exactly when the inclusion induces a surjection on full-group abelianizations. In both constructions, the embedded commutator subgroup has a unique maximal overgroup in the ambient commutator subgroup, namely its normalizer. For Cantor minimal systems, the factor construction yields partition stabilizers of the type in the Grigorchuk-Vorobets conjecture. The subgroupoid normalizers act topologically primitively. Groupoid homology makes the criteria computable for these systems and shifts of finite type. Examples include finitely generated nonsimple and locally finite simple maximal subgroups of infinite index in finitely generated infinite simple amenable groups.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matui

item.title: Banach Gelfand Triples with Kernel Theorems via Equivalence Bimodules
item.description: arXiv:2609.37780v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hilbert C*-modules whose coefficient C*-algebra is equipped with a finite faithful trace generate Banach Gelfand triples. This provides a natural setting for the interpretation of Hilbert C*-modules as function spaces. In particular, when the modules are finitely generated and projective, their external tensor products interact well with projective tensor products. This allowed us to derive abstract kernel theorems for Hilbert C*-modules. As an application, we apply our results to Heisenberg modules and obtain new kernel theorems for time-frequency analysis.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Bytchenkoff, Arvin Lamando, Franz Luef

item.title: Kadison-Kastler Distance and Interior Angle for Masas: Connections with Entropy and Probabilistic Index
item.description: arXiv:2609.38206v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Kadison--Kastler distance and the interior angle between masas in finite-dimensional matrix algebras. In \(\mathbb{M}_2(\mathbb{C})\), we obtain an explicit formula for the Kadison--Kastler distance between two masas and show that every value in \([0,1]\) is attained by \(\mathrm{d}_{\textrm{KK}}(\Delta,u\Delta u^*)\). We further prove that the distance attains its maximal value precisely when the relative unitary is a Hadamard unitary. In addition, for every $v$ in the groupoid normaliser of $\Delta$, the Kadison--Kastler distance between \(\Delta\) and \(v\Delta v^*\) assumes either its minimal or maximal possible value. We also establish the identity \[ \mathrm{d}_{\textrm{KK}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})=\sin\alpha(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}) \] for any two intermediate subalgebras \(\mathbb{C}\subsetneq\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}\subsetneq\mathbb{M}_2(\mathbb{C})\). Most notably, for any unitaries \(u,v\in\mathbb{M}_2(\mathbb{C})\), we establish the equivalence of maximal Kadison--Kastler distance, maximal interior angle, maximal Connes--St\o rmer modified entropy, and minimal Popa probabilistic index: \[ \mathrm{d}_{\textrm{KK}}(u\Delta u^*,v\Delta v^*)=1 \iff h(u\Delta u^*,v\Delta v^*)=\log 2 \iff \alpha(u\Delta u^*,v\Delta v^*)=\frac{\pi}{2} \iff \lambda(u\Delta u^*,v\Delta v^*)=\frac{1}{2}. \] For general \(\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})\), we prove a unitary invariance property for the interior angle and derive an explicit formula for the angle between arbitrary masas of the form \(u\Delta^{(n)}u^*\) and \(v\Delta^{(n)}v^*\). As a consequence, the interior angle is \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) precisely when the relative unitary \(u^*v\) is a Hadamard unitary. Finally, we show that every value in \(\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) is attained as the interior angle between a pair of masas in \(\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})\).
item.dc:creator: Indrajit Ghosh, Sumit Kumar

item.title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15253v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matui
